reasons: Missing-clause finding is substantiated: Section 17(b) only obliges Sparkling (us) to cease use and return/destroy Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes, and the survival list (Section 18) contains nothing on exit assistance or data return, so the agreement is silent on Garman returning our data or providing migration help.

Direction is correct for our side: the inserted 17(d) places the obligations on Garman (Vendor/Licensor) and runs in favour of Sparkling (Customer/Licensee), including the data converted under Section 4(b).

Insert tracks the preferred position closely and completely — up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty days, and subsequent deletion with written certification — with no extraneous edits to existing text (minimal-edit test met).

Placement as a new subsection (d) within Section 17 (Term and Termination), after 17(b)/(c) and before the survival provision, matches the redline guidance; the survival clause is non-exhaustive ("include but are not limited to") and expressly covers provisions contemplating post-termination performance, so no conforming amendment there is strictly necessary.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position, explains the gap (silence on our converted data under Section 4(b)) and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing.

Minor, non-blocking: the anchor paragraph p0129 is shown as "not yet rendered," so exact adjacency/lettering (assumes p0129 is 17(c)) should be confirmed on final rendering; optionally add Section 17(d) to the Section 18 survival enumeration for belt-and-braces.
